Class ClassChangeEvent

java.lang.Object
java.util.EventObject
io.micronaut.context.event.ApplicationEvent
io.micronaut.context.reload.ClassChangeEvent
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class ClassChangeEvent extends ApplicationEvent
The application's classes changed: a development launcher compiled them into a new generation of the application classloader and is about to replace the beans of the retired generation.

The event is published before any bean is touched. Listeners use it to forget cached state about classes of the retired generation: a cache keyed by class evicts every key for which isStaleType(Class) holds. Registries built from beans (routes, scheduled jobs, message consumers) do not listen here; they watch the beans they are built from and receive the change as a batch. Listeners that need the exact classes look at changes().

The launcher publishes the event in a restart as well, to the context being stopped, so that beans carried over to the next context can clean up what they cached about the retired classes.

Since:
5.3.0

graemerocher
